I committed the RB2 merge as c50c7ab (condensed into 8251007) with the requested message. All verification steps passed; nothing was pushed, and nothing under scratch: lanes was touched.

How the conflicts were resolved

  • tests/test_lattice.py:
    • I removed the test lane's expanded Bloch/scale/split/inversion/periodicity test, following RB2's removal of the older version. The two Rust property tests RB2 named cover everything it checked, and both exist and pass after the merge.
    • I kept the lane's markers on the derivative test and applied RB2's reduction to the (1, -1) and (3, 1) orders. The dropped orders are covered by ewald_complete_derivative and ewald_derivative_identities, which also pass.
    • I kept the physics marker on the out-of-plane-shift test. It sat inside the conflict block and would otherwise have been lost.
    • The docstring now says "public-path derivatives", because PA2 removed the pyfunction RB2's wording referred to.
  • tests/test_lattice_sum_adjoints.py: I used the lane's variable naming with RB2's corrected split check: the full sum stays fixed at 0.9 and the parts are traced at 1.2.
  • tests/test_geometry_misc.py:
    • I removed the reciprocal-duality test, as RB2 did. The Rust reciprocal_duality test covers it.
    • I kept the lane's skew-diffraction test. Its comment named a Rust test RB2 removed, so it now points to diffraction_orders_are_complete_paired_and_unique.
    • I kept the lane's Brillouin, kz-branch and helicity-index tests, and added RB2's hexagonal Brillouin test with a physics marker.

Xfails converted: none. Both out-of-plane-shift cases still fail as expected after RB2, so they and their docs/status.md entry stay. The hexagonal Brillouin bug was never pinned as an xfail on the integration branch.

The parity result matches RB2's own PASS, so there were no lattice-case changes to explain. It reports the previous commit hash because it ran before the commit, but it used the freshly built merged extension.

The scratchpad directory is shared with other agents, and a lane-rc run overwrote my first pytest log. I threw those logs away and re-ran clippy, cargo test and pytest into a private subdirectory; the numbers above come from those re-runs.
